text:
mike: heads-up — p95 shot up on dedicated-nyc-g1 around 11:12 UTC, correlated with a single tenant. graphs in #alerts show a sharp step, not gradual.

sara: saw that, digging. latency from 120ms -> 1.2s for generation requests. throughput also dropped by ~30% on the pool.

mike: infra-bot posted an alert: <https://alerts.internal/release/INC-1223|INC-1223> — noisy tenant + KV cache churn mentioned.

infra-bot: alert: pool=dedicated-nyc-g1 metric=latency.p95 value=1189ms change=+900% impacted_tenant=tenant-42

carla: quick hypothesis — we had a prompt-length spike from that tenant earlier, many requests with long prefixes followed by streaming tool-calls. Could be kernel selection fallback for long sequences + streaming backpressure.

ryan: profiler dump from one affected worker:
```
[profiler] seq_len_distribution: 1..64: 78% | 65..512: 20% | >512: 2%
[kernel_select] chosen_kernel="matmul_opt_v2" fallback_kernel="matmul_generic" reason="seq_len_mismatch"
[kv_cache] entries_evicted=312 miss_rate=0.38 prefix_cache_hits=0.12
[batching] avg_batch_size=4 avg_wait_ms=26 max_wait_ms=120
```

sara: interesting — the distribution shows a fat tail. but kernel_select claims v2 then fallback_generic. that fallback is expensive for attention calls.

mike: logs show repeated tool-call loops from tenant-42: user -> tool -> user -> tool in a tight loop, streaming each time. that means many short incremental inputs but also some very long history being streamed back, which thrashes the KV cache.

carla: that combination explains both higher per-token compute (generic kernel) and bursting batches with high wait times (streaming backpressure). KV evictions cause regen of cached KV which spikes work.

ryan: quick repro command we ran:
```
# replay trace from tenant-42 for 10s
python tools/replay_trace.py --trace traces/tenant-42-20260211.json --rate 200
```

sara: mitigation options:
- temporarily pin kernel selection to `matmul_opt_v2` for model=vicuna-7b@sha123 for this pool
- increase KV cache size for dedicated-nyc-g1 (reduce eviction)
- throttle tool-calls per-session or enforce streaming window limits
- lower max_wait_ms so batches flush faster (reduce latency spike)

mike: I'd prefer non-invasive first: kernel pin + throttle rules for tenant-42. Carla can you push the kernel pin as a short rollback-safe change?

carla: on it. will push a canary to two nodes and monitor. also adding a local KV cache size bump for canary nodes.

infra-bot: deploy started: change=pin-kernel-matmul_opt_v2 scope=dedicated-nyc-g1 canary_nodes=2

ryan: after canary, p95 dropped back to ~160ms on those nodes. overall pool p95 improved to ~320ms. good signal.

sara: filed an action item to add heuristic: if seq_len tail > X% and streaming_detected then prefer stable kernel (avoid generic fallback), and mark as perf-regression candidate for model onboarding.

mike: one more note — tenant was using excessive function/tool calls per request (avg 6), we should add a quota and a short circuit in the router to detect tool loops and return 429 + guidance.

carla: created PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/merge_requests/2345 — pins kernel + KV bump + emergency tenant throttle. will keep the tenant throttled until we deploy a better batching heuristic.

mike: thanks. please post follow-up with perf graphs and root-cause doc. marking incident resolved-for-now. :white_check_mark:

ryan: will add a small perf test to CI that replays mixed-length traces to catch kernel selection fallbacks.

infra-bot: incident INC-1223 status -> monitored
